nodes.summary: The labels of the transition system: `prepare n` (send the prepare request $n$), `promise a n r` (acceptor $a$ answers it, reporting $r$), `propose n v S` (issue the proposal $(n, v)$, justified by the responses of the quorum $S$) and `accept a n v` (acceptor $a$ accepts it). Their effects are given by the steps.
nodes.title: Actions of single-decree Paxos

nodes.summary: The proposal numbered `b` with value `v` is chosen when every acceptor of some quorum accepted it (Lamport, *Paxos Made Simple*, Section 2.2: "A value is chosen when a single proposal with that value has been accepted by a majority of the acceptors").
nodes.title: Chosen proposal

nodes.summary: In every state reachable from the initial state of single-decree Paxos, two chosen values are equal. Acceptances are never withdrawn, so a value chosen once stays chosen, and no other value is chosen later in the same run.
nodes.title: Paxos safety: at most one value is chosen

nodes.summary: In every Paxos voting history, two chosen values are equal: the second safety requirement of Section 2.1, "Only a single value is chosen".
nodes.title: At most one value is chosen

nodes.summary: In a Paxos voting history, the value $v$ is chosen when, for some proposal number $b$, the proposal $(b, v)$ is chosen: every acceptor of some quorum accepted it.
nodes.title: Chosen value

nodes.summary: `r` is the highest-numbered proposal with number less than `n` that acceptor `a` accepted in `votes`, or `none` if there is none.
nodes.title: Highest-numbered acceptance below a number

nodes.summary: The initial state: nothing sent, nothing accepted, no promise made.
nodes.title: Initial state of single-decree Paxos

nodes.summary: The inductive invariant of single-decree Paxos holds in the initial state, where every set of messages and acceptances is empty.
nodes.title: The Paxos invariant holds initially

nodes.summary: Every state reachable from the initial state of single-decree Paxos satisfies the inductive invariant. This is CSLib's `mtrInv_of_trInv` applied to the invariant, which holds initially and is preserved by every step.
nodes.title: The Paxos invariant holds in every reachable state

nodes.summary: If a state satisfies the inductive invariant, so does the state after any step. The two delicate cases are these.
nodes.title: Every step of single-decree Paxos preserves the invariant

nodes.summary: Acceptances are of issued proposals; proposal numbers are unique; an acceptor that responded to the prepare request `n` has `maxBal ≥ n` and its report is still its highest acceptance below `n`; every issued proposal is justified by responses of a quorum under the value rule.
nodes.title: The inductive invariant of single-decree Paxos

nodes.summary: Single-decree Paxos, for a quorum system, is the CSLib labelled transition system (`Cslib.LTS`) whose states are Paxos states, whose labels are actions and whose transitions are the steps. Reachability is CSLib's `CanReach` from the initial state.
nodes.title: Single-decree Paxos as a CSLib labelled transition system

nodes.summary: Majorities form a quorum system (Lamport, *Paxos Made Simple*, Section 2.2): the quorums are the sets containing more than half of the finitely many acceptors.
nodes.title: Majorities form a quorum system

nodes.summary: In every Paxos voting history: if the proposal numbered $m$ with value $v$ is chosen, then every proposal issued with a number $n > m$ has value $v$.
nodes.title: Lamport's P2b

nodes.summary: In every state reachable from the initial state of single-decree Paxos, a chosen value is the value of some issued proposal: the first safety requirement of Section 2.1.
nodes.title: Paxos safety: only a proposed value is chosen

nodes.summary: Only a proposed value is chosen (Lamport, *Paxos Made Simple*, Section 2.1, first safety requirement).
nodes.title: Only a proposed value is chosen

nodes.summary: A family of finite sets of acceptors, the quorums, any two of which share an acceptor (Lamport, *Paxos Made Simple*, Section 2.2: "any two majorities have at least one acceptor in common", and the "obvious generalization of a majority").
nodes.title: Quorum system

nodes.summary: Lamport's value rule (Phase 2(a)): every response of the acceptors in `S` to the prepare request `n` reports nothing, or `v` is the value of the highest-numbered reported proposal.
nodes.title: Lamport's value rule

nodes.summary: The sent prepare requests, the number of the highest prepare request each acceptor responded to, the sent promises (responses to prepare requests), the issued proposals (accept requests), and the acceptances.
nodes.title: State of the single-decree Paxos algorithm

nodes.summary: The transitions of single-decree Paxos, one per action, for a quorum system:
nodes.title: One step of single-decree Paxos

nodes.summary: Chosen value in a state (Section 2.2): every acceptor of some quorum accepted a proposal with value `v`, all with the same number.
nodes.title: Chosen value in a state

nodes.summary: In every state of single-decree Paxos satisfying the inductive invariant, the issued proposals and the acceptances form a Paxos voting history. In particular P2c holds over the whole history: the quorum that justified a proposal under Lamport's value rule witnesses it, because the reports of its acceptors are still their highest acceptances below the proposal number.
nodes.title: Reachable states are Paxos voting histories

nodes.summary: A Paxos voting history, for a quorum system on acceptors and a type of values, consists of two relations: `proposed b v`, a proposal numbered $b \in \mathbb{N}$ with value $v$ was issued, and `voted a b v`, acceptor $a$ accepted it. They must satisfy:
nodes.title: A Paxos voting history

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
